name: King of Edom
overview: The King of Edom was a male monarch who ruled Edom during the reign of King Zedekiah of Judah, as recorded in Jeremiah 27:3. Beyond his role as king during this period, no additional personal or tribal details are provided in Scripture. His presence is noted in the context of geopolitical relations involving Judah.
namesAndTitles: This individual is identified by the title 'King of Edom,' which straightforwardly means 'king of Edom.' This title is not a personal name but a designation of his royal office over the Edomite people, as noted in Jeremiah 27:3.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for the King of Edom beyond his status as king during Zedekiah's reign. No additional familial connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Edom's significance lies in his role as a contemporary ruler during the reign of Judah's King Zedekiah, highlighting the political landscape surrounding Judah at that time. His mention in Jeremiah 27:3 situates him among neighboring kings who were engaged in the events unfolding during this critical period in Judah's history. Though details are sparse, his inclusion underscores the interconnectedness of regional powers in the biblical narrative.
